focus: Pi: hooks, tool names, install/update/rollback, compaction path, deny/rewrite/replace, subagent handling, project source, skills, v1 footprint

findings.claim: ADR-0004 still lists Q7 (Pi's in-process plugin mechanism for instructions.md) as an open question, but TECH-SPEC already marks the same question decided.
findings.evidence: ADR-0004 line 3: 'Open details: Q2, Q7, Q10 and Q11 in TECH-SPEC §10.' ADR-0004 line 53: 'Pi runs as an in-process plugin, not over MCP. It gets the same instructions.md bytes through its single plugin mechanism. Which mechanism that is: Q7.' TECH-SPEC line 177: 'Pi (in-process plugin) | the same instructions.md bytes, appended to the system prompt in before_agent_start (Q7)'. TECH-SPEC line 414: '| Q7 | Pi: same instructions.md bytes via before_agent_start | [D] |'. Also a separate Q7 exists in DECISIONS-r3.md line 13 about retention/PID cap, a different topic -- the Q-numbers collide across docs, which makes 'Open details: Q2, Q7, Q10, Q11' ambiguous about which Q7 is meant.
findings.archaeology: n/a (doc process issue, not a code regression)
findings.fix: Update ADR-0004's status line to drop Q7 (it is decided per TECH-SPEC:414) or point directly at TECH-SPEC §10's Q7, and rename/renumber the DECISIONS-r3 Q7 so the same token is not reused for two unrelated questions.

findings.claim: TECH-SPEC describes Pi's before_agent_start mechanism as the instructions.md bytes being 'appended' to the system prompt, but the actual Pi extension API performs a full replace, not an append.
findings.evidence: Pi source packages/coding-agent/src/core/extensions/types.ts:1496-1499: 'export interface BeforeAgentStartEventResult { message?: ...; /** Replace the complete system prompt for this turn. Later handlers observe this exact override. */ systemPrompt?: string; }'. The event does carry the current prompt read-only (types.ts:934-935: 'readonly systemPrompt: string'), so an append effect is achievable only if the handler manually concatenates event.systemPrompt + new text before returning it as the full systemPrompt value -- there is no dedicated append field.
findings.archaeology: n/a (Pi is a third-party agent source, not v1 history)
findings.fix: Reword TECH-SPEC:177 to say the handler reads the current systemPrompt and returns the concatenated result as a full override, so a future implementer does not assume a dedicated append API exists and accidentally drops earlier handlers' prompt changes.

findings.claim: ADR-0008's 'isMCPReady' row says availability is known in-process for Pi, but gives no live check or evidence path specific to Pi for that claim (only v1 git history for the Node command-hook agents).
findings.evidence: ADR-0008 line 28: '`isMCPReady()`: a machine-global PID marker file | Claude Code: ... ; Pi, OpenCode 2: in-process, availability is known. Other agents: the server writes a ready row ...'. v1 archaeology: `git log -S isMCPReady --oneline` in cm-main shows the sentinel-file mechanism (04569b12 '#230', f4e8d2ac '#354', ff5b0cff '#844 #845 #846') was built and hardened entirely for the external, file-sentinel agents; none of those commits mention Pi, because v1 never had a Pi adapter. So the Pi row is a new, unverified claim with no v1 precedent and no LV check number attached (unlike LV7-LV10 elsewhere in the same ADR).
findings.archaeology: INTRODUCED_BY: 04569b12 'fix: graceful MCP redirect fallback via readiness sentinel (#230)', hardened by f4e8d2ac '(#354)' and ff5b0cff '(#844 #845 #846)'. ORIGINAL_INTENT (04569b12): the sentinel file exists because, for agents that spawn hooks as separate OS processes, the hook process has no other way to know the MCP server is up. REGRESSION_RISK: the Pi row assumes 'in-process, availability is known' needs no such mechanism; if that assumption is wrong (e.g. the plugin and the ctx server initialize in separate processes after all), the v1 bug class (#230 premature deny before MCP is ready) reappears for Pi with no test covering it. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: any Pi-specific readiness assumption must get its own live check (like LV7) before it is treated as settled.
findings.fix: Add an LV check for Pi's in-process readiness assumption (mirroring LV7), or cite the Pi extension API call that proves readiness is synchronously known, before relying on it to skip the sentinel-file mechanism.
